title: Long-Horizon Memory and Safety: Do Agents with Persistent Memory Develop More Dangerous Behavioral Patterns Over Time?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Directly tests whether persistent memory introduces emergent safety risks in deployed agentic systems. If safety failure rate increases with memory accumulation, this has immediate implications for production agent deployment policies.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running 100 sequential tasks with safety evaluations after every 10 tasks requires building a substantial agent infrastructure. Designing meaningful safety evaluations and 100 diverse tasks is a heavy lift for beginners. The persistent memory implementation adds engineering complexity.

narrow_scope.reasoning: 100 sequential tasks with periodic evaluation is ambitious for 30 hours. Multiple confounds (task ordering, memory retrieval quality) make it hard to isolate the memory effect. No clear minimal first deliverable.
